mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר for הקדש and the meaning of his argument with רבי ישמעאל, then אביי's contradiction between paying from מיטב and paying with anything worth money.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. If רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר for הקדש were about someone who promised money to the Temple, הקדש would be a mere בעל חוב, who collects only from בינונית. The קל וחומר would also be breakable, since an ordinary person is stronger in damages than הקדש. So the גמרא explains that the case is an ordinary ox goring a הקדש ox, and that רבי עקיבא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, who makes such an ox pay full damages. The גמרא then asks whether רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא might argue only about הקדש, and not about how land is appraised. It rejects this three times: from רבי עקיבא's words 'לא בא הכתוב', from his 'קל וחומר להקדש', and from an explicit ברייתא quoted by רב אשי. Next, אביי points out a contradiction to רבא: the פסוק says payment comes from מיטב, but a ברייתא says anything worth money, even bran, is acceptable. רבא answers that one who pays willingly may use anything, while one forced by בית דין pays from his best land. עולא supports this from the word ישלם, but אביי rejects that proof. אביי then starts a new answer modeled on a ברייתא about a landowner who may take מעשר עני up to half: his land lost value only because buyers see he is desperate for cash.

steps.title: A creditor only collects from medium land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: if הקדש is treated like a creditor, it should collect only from בינונית, not from עידית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a creditor collects only from medium-quality land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an objection it began just before this. If the case is a person who promised money to הקדש, הקדש is just like a creditor, and a creditor collects from medium land, not the best land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר ends with הקדש collecting from עידית. If הקדש here is only an ordinary creditor, the normal rule of בעל חוב בבינונית should apply instead. So this explanation of רבי עקיבא does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
Medium-quality land, which a creditor collects from
The best-quality land, which damages are paid from

phrases.english: And a creditor collects from medium-quality land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection, begun before this section, to reading רבי עקיבא as speaking about a pledge to הקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר is about someone who promised money to הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pledge makes הקדש a creditor, and a creditor collects only from בינונית, so the קל וחומר's ending of עידית cannot fit.

steps.title: Even if a creditor collects from the best land, the logic still fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer. Even if רבי עקיבא held a creditor collects from עידית, the קל וחומר can be broken, since a creditor has a strength in damages that הקדש lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say רבי עקיבא holds a creditor also collects from the best land, the reasoning can still be broken. A creditor is an ordinary person, whose power is strong in damages. Can you say the same about הקדש, whose power is weak in damages?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to answer that maybe רבי עקיבא thinks creditors collect from the best land too. It says that even then, the קל וחומר does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the starting case is weaker than the case we compare it to. An ordinary person gets paid when his ox is damaged, but הקדש does not (because of 'שור רעהו'). Since the ordinary creditor is stronger in this area, we cannot learn 'all the more so' for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a possible answer)
It can be refuted, the קל וחומר can be broken
His power was strengthened
Its power was weakened
Damages

steps.confusionAlert: 'Weakened in damages' does not mean הקדש can't collect debts. It means the תורה does not make others pay when they damage a הקדש ox (based on 'שור רעהו').

phrases.english: And if you will say that Rabbi Akiva holds:
a creditor also collects from the best land;
it can still be refuted:
what about an ordinary creditor?
His power is strengthened in damages,
phrases.notes: An ordinary person gets paid when someone's ox damages his property.

phrases.english: will you say the same about הקדש,
whose power is weakened in damages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against the challenge of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense, that רבי עקיבא holds a creditor also collects from עידית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר from a creditor to הקדש fails (פירכא), because a creditor is stronger than הקדש in damages.

steps.title: The case is our ox goring an ox of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. רבי עקיבא speaks about an ordinary ox that gored a הקדש ox. The 'שור רעהו' problem is solved because he follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is that our ox gored an ox of הקדש. As for your difficulty that the תורה said 'his fellow's ox', and not an ox of הקדש: רבי עקיבא holds like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'pledge' explanation and offers a new case: an ordinary person's ox damaged a הקדש ox. It also answers the problem from the פסוק 'שור רעהו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this case seemed impossible, because 'שור רעהו' seemed to exempt damage to a הקדש ox. The גמרא says רבי עקיבא does not read the פסוק that way, since he agrees with רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. So damage to הקדש is paid, and the קל וחומר makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (returning to an earlier idea)
Our ox, an ordinary person's ox
His fellow's ox (שמות 21:35)
The Merciful One, the תורה

phrases.english: Really, it is where our ox gored
an ox of הקדש.
And what was difficult for you:
the Merciful One said 'his fellow's ox',
and not an ox of הקדש;
Rabbi Akiva holds
like Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דִּנְגַח תּוֹרָא דִידַן לְתוֹרָא דְהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pledge explanation fails, the גמרא goes back to the ox-goring case and removes its difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case and assigns רבי עקיבא to a תנא who has a different reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'שור רעהו' exempts damage to a הקדש ox, so רבי עקיבא could not mean that case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: damage to a הקדש ox is paid, so the קל וחומר is about that case.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's ruling on oxes of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. A הקדש ox that gores is exempt, but an ordinary ox that gores a הקדש ox pays full damages, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says, a הקדש ox that gored an ordinary person's ox is exempt. An ordinary person's ox that gored a הקדש ox, whether it is a תם or a מועד, pays full damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the opinion that רבי עקיבא follows. It shows that damage to a הקדש ox is paid in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is one-sided. When הקדש's ox damages, nobody pays. When an ordinary ox damages הקדש, the owner pays full damages, even for a תם, which usually pays only half. This supports the answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person (not הקדש)
An ox with no history of goring, which normally pays half damages
A warned ox that has gored before, which pays full damages
Full damages

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר is about an ordinary ox goring a הקדש ox. He holds like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: such damage is paid in full, even by a תם.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט –
phrases.english: an ox of הקדש that gored an ordinary person's ox
is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: an ordinary person's ox that gored an ox of הקדש,
whether it is a תם or a מועד,
pays full damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא behind the opinion that step 3 says רבי עקיבא follows.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a view under which damage to a הקדש ox is paid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: an ordinary ox that gores a הקדש ox pays full damages, whether תם or מועד.

steps.title: Maybe they argue only about הקדש, not about which land is appraised
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, the גמרא suggests a new reading. Maybe everyone agrees we appraise by the land of the ניזק, and the only argument is whether an ordinary ox that damages הקדש must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how do we know that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about the case where the ניזק's best land equals the מזיק's worst land? Maybe everyone agrees that we appraise by the ניזק's land, and they argue about the dispute between רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and the רבנן. רבי עקיבא holds like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, and רבי ישמעאל holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against the earlier way of reading the argument. It suggests the two תנאים may not disagree about land quality at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we assumed רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about appraising עידית. Once we say רבי עקיבא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, there could be a simpler reading. Both agree on how land is appraised, and they disagree only about whether הקדש collects damages from an ordinary ox.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you just said is true
The best-quality land
The worst-quality land
We appraise by the land of the injured party
The Sages, who disagree with רבי שמעון בן מנסיא

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion. In the next three steps the גמרא rejects it, so the original reading of the argument stands.

phrases.english: If so,
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva –
from where do we know that about the best land of the injured party
and the worst land of the damager they argue?
phrases.notes: This is the case where the injured party's best land is only as good as the damager's worst land. That was the earlier way of explaining their argument.

phrases.english: Perhaps everyone agrees
that we appraise by the injured party's land,
and here, in the dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא וְרַבָּנַן קָמִפַּלְגִי –
phrases.english: of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya and the Rabbis is where they argue –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya,
and Rabbi Yishmael holds like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from Steps 3-4 (רבי עקיבא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא) to question the whole basis of the argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree about appraising the ניזק's עידית against the מזיק's זיבורית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי עקיבא's position can be explained by his view on הקדש, the argument might be only about הקדש, with no disagreement about land appraisal.

steps.title: First rejection: רבי עקיבא's words 'the verse comes only'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי עקיבא said 'לא בא הכתוב', which shows he disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about how to read the פסוק on appraising land.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the meaning of 'the verse comes only'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the new suggestion. It points to רבי עקיבא's own words in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רבי עקיבא says 'לא בא הכתוב', he is arguing about what the פסוק teaches about appraisal. He says it teaches that damages are collected from עידית. If he agreed with רבי ישמעאל on appraisal, he would have no reason to argue about the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your suggestion were true
The verse comes only to teach; a way of arguing about what a פסוק means

phrases.english: If so,
what is the meaning of "the verse comes only"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַאי לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree about land appraisal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא's wording 'לא בא הכתוב' shows he disputes the reading of the פסוק on appraisal. So they must argue about appraisal.

steps.title: Second rejection: the קל וחומר for הקדש would make no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second proof. רבי עקיבא learned הקדש's rule through a קל וחומר. A קל וחומר only works if he is talking about how land is collected, not if הקדש is already stricter as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what is the meaning of 'a קל וחומר for הקדש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason to reject the suggestion, again from רבי עקיבא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned הקדש's rule from ordinary people through a קל וחומר, which means he is talking about collecting from עידית. If his point were only the view of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, הקדש would already be stricter, since even a תם pays in full. Then there would be no need for a קל וחומר at all. So the original reading stands, and they argue about appraising land.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; a second difficulty
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Property belonging to the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue only about הקדש is already rejected twice, from 'לא בא הכתוב' and from 'קל וחומר להקדש'. The next step adds a third and final rejection.

phrases.english: And furthermore,
what is the meaning of "and a fortiori for consecrated property"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent rejection of Step 5's suggestion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי עקיבא's position is only about the view of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא on הקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's view, הקדש is already stricter than an ordinary person. So the קל וחומר would be pointless, and רבי עקיבא's words must be about appraisal of land.

steps.title: An explicit ברייתא shows that רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל argue about whose land is meant
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא that openly says רבי ישמעאל reads מיטב as the ניזק's best land and רבי עקיבא reads it as the מזיק's best land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, רב אשי said it is taught openly in a ברייתא: 'The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay.' רבי ישמעאל says this means the best field and vineyard of the ניזק. רבי עקיבא says it means the best field and vineyard of the מזיק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third and final reason to reject the idea from Step 5 that everyone agrees about appraising land. A ברייתא says in plain words that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 7 proved the argument from רבי עקיבא's wording and his קל וחומר. Here no proof from wording is needed, because a ברייתא states both opinions outright. So the suggestion that the only argument is about הקדש is fully rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught openly, in plain words, in a ברייתא
The best, the highest-quality land
The one who was damaged
The one who caused the damage and must pay

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, מיטב is measured by the ניזק's land. According to רבי עקיבא, payment comes from the מזיק's best land. This is a real argument, and it is not only about הקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'his' in 'his field' points to different people in each opinion. For רבי ישמעאל it means the ניזק's field. For רבי עקיבא it means the מזיק's field.

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Rav Ashi say:
It is taught explicitly in a baraita:
"The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay"
the best of the field of the injured party,
and the best of the vineyard of the injured party;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
the best of the field of the one who caused the damage,
and the best of the vineyard of the one who caused the damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, תַּנְיָא בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and final rejection of the suggestion from Step 5, after the proofs in Steps 6 and 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree about appraising by the ניזק's land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An explicit ברייתא states that they argue about whose land is meant by מיטב.

steps.title: אביי begins a contradiction: the פסוק says payment must be from the best land
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings the first side of a contradiction to רבא. The פסוק of מיטב suggests that only best land counts as payment and nothing else does.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי pointed out a contradiction to רבא. It is written: 'The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay.' This means best land, yes, but anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. אביי sets up the first side of a contradiction: reading the פסוק, a מזיק may pay only with his best land. This step prepares the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he shall pay from the best' seem to limit the payment. If the תורה names מיטב, that suggests other kinds of payment are not accepted. The second side, which clashes with this, comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He threw, meaning he pointed out two sources that seem to clash
Something else, any other kind of payment

phrases.english: Abaye raised a contradiction to Rava:
It is written: "The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay"
best land, yes; something else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about what kinds of payment a מזיק may give.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the פסוק simply, payment must come from מיטב and not from other things.

steps.title: A ברייתא says anything worth money, even bran, may be used to pay
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word ישיב that a מזיק may pay with anything worth money, even bran. That clashes with the פסוק of מיטב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the word 'he shall pay back' comes to include anything worth money, even bran!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the second side of the contradiction. A ברייתא allows payment with any item worth money, even cheap bran.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 suggested that only best land is allowed. This ברייתא says even something very low in value, like bran, is fine as long as it is worth money. Both cannot be true at once without some explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall pay back, a word from the פסוק of the pit
To include, to add an extra case
Something worth money, even if it is not actual money
Bran, the husks left over from grain, which are worth very little

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "He shall pay back"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:34, from the case of the pit.

phrases.english: comes to include anything worth money,
and even bran!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's contradiction by bringing the clashing ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the פסוק of מיטב as limiting payment to best land only.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows any item worth money, even bran, so payment cannot be limited to best land.

steps.title: Paying willingly versus paying when forced
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a מזיק who pays on his own may use anything worth money. A מזיק who pays only when forced by בית דין must pay from his best land.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here it is when he pays willingly. There it is when he pays against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves אביי's contradiction by showing that each source is about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of ישיב, which allows even bran, is about a מזיק who pays on his own. The פסוק of מיטב is about a מזיק who refused and had to be taken to בית דין. Because he made trouble for the ניזק, he must pay with his best land.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no real contradiction
Willingly, on his own choice
Against his will, when forced by בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: A מזיק who pays willingly may pay with anything worth money, even bran. A מזיק who has to be forced by בית דין pays from his מיטב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two different levels of payment, depending on whether the מזיק cooperates or must be forced.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, when he pays of his own will,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of ישיב, which allows even bran.

phrases.english: there, when he pays against his will.
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק of מיטב, when בית דין makes him pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן מִדַּעְתּוֹ, כָּאן בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק and the ברייתא seemed to give opposite rules for every payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying willingly allows anything worth money. Paying when forced requires מיטב.

steps.title: Support from the word 'he shall pay'
steps.stepSummary: עולא בריה דרב עילאי says the פסוק's word ישלם supports רבא, because it means paying against one's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא, son of רב עילאי, said: The wording also fits, because it says 'he shall pay', which means against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings support for רבא's answer from Step 11. He points to the word ישלם in the פסוק of מיטב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that only a מזיק forced by בית דין must pay from his best land. עולא reads ישלם as describing forced payment. That would explain why this פסוק demands מיטב.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, meaning the text itself supports the point
He shall pay
Against his will, forced

phrases.english: Ulla, son of Rav Ilai, said:
The wording is also precise,
as it is written: "he shall pay", meaning against his will.
phrases.notes: This is the word at the end of the מיטב פסוק, שמות 22:4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer from the wording of the פסוק
steps.raayaObject: רבא's distinction that a forced payer must pay from מיטב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word ישלם in the פסוק, read as forced payment

steps.title: אביי: 'he shall pay' sounds voluntary
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects עולא's proof. The text says ישלם, 'he shall pay', not ישולם, 'he shall be paid', so it sounds like paying willingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does it say 'it shall be paid'? It says 'he shall pay', which suggests he pays on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away עולא's support. He argues the word actually points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A passive word like ישולם would suggest someone else makes him pay. The active word ישלם shows the מזיק himself paying, which sounds voluntary. So the word ישלם gives no support to רבא's answer, and אביי goes on to offer a different answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall be paid (passive form)
Of his own will, voluntarily
Implies, suggests

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is it written "he shall be paid"?!
"He shall pay" is written,
which implies of his own will!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in Step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only עולא's proof from the word ישלם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The active form ישלם suggests voluntary payment, not forced payment

steps.title: אביי's new answer, modeled on the poor man's tithe ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a different answer, following how מר (his teacher) explained a ברייתא. A person who owns land but cannot sell it may be fed מעשר עני up to half its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is like the Master's approach. A ברייתא teaches: Someone who has houses, fields, and vineyards but cannot find buyers is fed from מעשר עני, up to half.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new answer to the contradiction between מיטב and ישיב. He first quotes the ברייתא that his model is based on, so this step sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets someone with property but no cash take מעשר עני, but only up to half the value of his property. The Master explained that ברייתא in a certain way. אביי will use the same kind of explanation for paying damages.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the Master, following his teacher's approach
Poor man's tithe, given to the needy
Up to half

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It is like the Master's approach,
phrases.notes: מר means 'the Master.' אביי is borrowing the way his teacher solved a different problem.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who had
houses, fields, and vineyards,
but cannot find buyers to sell them to,
we feed him from the poor man's tithe,
up to half.
phrases.notes: Half of what his property is worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting עולא's support, אביי opens a different answer to the contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Model answer borrowed from a parallel case (מעשר עני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's split between voluntary and forced payment, supported by ישלם
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer will follow the Master's explanation of the מעשר עני ברייתא, which the גמרא now begins to develop

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The Master asks what situation leaves the man unable to sell. He suggests a first possibility: all land in the area became cheap, including his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master discussed it: What is the case? If everyone's land became cheap, and his became cheap along with theirs...
steps.whatsHappening: The Master asks what exact situation the ברייתא describes. He offers a first option, which the next step will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To understand the 'up to half' limit, we must know why he cannot sell. The first option is a general drop in land prices that hits his land too.

keyTerms.meaning: And he discussed it, worked through it
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Lands
Became cheap

phrases.english: And the Master discussed it:
What are the circumstances?
If everyone's land became cheap,
phrases.notes: Some versions read the word in round brackets, others the one in square brackets. Either way it means 'became cheap.'

phrases.english: and his also became cheap along with theirs,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the ברייתא quoted in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation in which the landowner cannot sell his property

steps.title: If all land became cheap, he should get even more
steps.stepSummary: The first option is rejected. If all land dropped in value, he is truly poor and should get more than half.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...then let him be given even much more, since everyone's land is cheap too!
steps.whatsHappening: The Master shows that the first option cannot be what the ברייתא means. In that case there would be no reason for the 'up to half' limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If prices fell everywhere, his land really is worth little now, so he truly counts as poor. A real poor person may take as much מעשר עני as he needs. The ברייתא's limit of half shows it must be talking about a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: A lot, much more
Let them feed him

phrases.english: then let them feed him even much more,
since everyone's land is cheap too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible case suggested in Step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the case where all land dropped in value
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case his land really is worth little, so there is no reason to stop at half

steps.title: Only his land dropped because buyers see he needs cash
steps.stepSummary: The Master gives the real case: land prices rose everywhere, but his field lost value because people can tell he is desperate for money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where everyone else's land went up in value. His own land, since people see him running around trying to raise money, went down in value.
steps.whatsHappening: The Master (מר) answers his own question from Step 15 with a second option, now that the first was rejected. The man's land is cheap only for him, because buyers know he is desperate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, if all land was cheap, the man would be truly poor and should get more than half. Here the land itself is still worth a lot, since prices around him went up. Only his personal situation lowers the offers, so he is not truly poor. This is the case where the ברייתא limits him to מעשר עני up to half.

keyTerms.meaning: went up in price, became expensive
lands, fields
goes in and goes out; keeps running around
money (literally, zuz coins)
went down in price, became cheap

steps.whatToRemember: The man who may take מעשר עני up to half his land's value owns land that is still really worth a lot. Only his desperation makes buyers offer less, so he is not fully poor.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 16. There, all land became cheap, so he would truly be poor. Here, only his land seems cheap, and only because buyers see that he needs cash fast.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines exactly which landowner the ברייתא means. אביי will use this case as the model for his new answer to the contradiction between מיטב and ישיב.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where it went up in price,
the land of everyone else,
and his own: since he goes in and goes out for money,
phrases.notes: He means that people see him running around trying to raise cash, so they figure he will accept a low offer.

phrases.english: his land went down in price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 16 rejected the first option, this step gives the second option as the correct answer to the question asked in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation does a landowner find that he cannot sell his land, so that he may take מעשר עני up to half its value?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Land prices went up for everyone, but his land lost value because buyers see that he is desperate for money and offer him less.
